question: In which of the following pathologies does a multineuropathy occur ?:
analysis: Multineuropathy, also known as mononeuritis multiplex, is a condition where multiple peripheral nerves are affected, often in an asymmetric pattern. This condition is commonly associated with vasculitis of the vasa nervorum, which leads to inflammation and damage to the blood vessels supplying the nerves. Diabetes mellitus can cause peripheral neuropathy, but it typically presents as a symmetric polyneuropathy rather than multineuropathy. Multiple sclerosis primarily affects the central nervous system, not peripheral nerves. Carpal tunnel syndrome is a mononeuropathy affecting the median nerve. Therefore, the most appropriate pathology associated with multineuropathy is vasculitis of the vasa nervorum.
